name: Writesonic
subcategory: AI drafting, research and content optimization
tagline: Draft researched articles and marketing copy with source links and revision controls

pricing.notes: Entry individual rate before promotions; generation limits vary.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Writesonic, draft researched articles and marketing copy with source links and revision controls. The hard boundary is integrated research, seo data, publishing workflows, and model routing, plus workflow, data, and model tuning.
coreLoopDIY: Take a brief, gather user-supplied source material, generate structured article and marketing copy drafts, and keep source links, citations, and revisions attached to each section.
whatYouLose: integrated research, SEO data, publishing workflows, and model routing
ongoingBurden: prompt maintenance, retrieval quality, source handling, provider changes, and editorial QA
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Writesonic because the subscription bundles a refined workflow, proprietary signals, templates, and predictable output quality for a team. The recurring cost buys prompt maintenance, retrieval quality, source handling, provider changes, and editorial QA, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Open WebUI
priorArt.desc: Active open-source interface for local and API-backed language models with retrieval features.

alternatives.name: AnythingLLM
alternatives.desc: A local AI workspace that keeps sources beside the draft, cites uploaded material, and turns recurring prompts into reusable agents.

facts.install: Desktop installer for macOS/Windows/Linux, or Docker for a self-hosted web instance
facts.engines: Local llama.cpp models plus Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI and many cloud APIs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter and Mistral
facts.dataFormat: Desktop data stays in the app's local storage; self-hosted data is stored in the mounted server storage and chosen vector database (LanceDB by default), while prompts sent to cloud models leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: It can generate source-grounded copy, but it lacks Writesonic's managed live-research article workflow, SEO controls, brand system, and publishing integrations.
facts.setupBlocker: The installer is easy, but useful results still require downloading a local model or supplying a model-provider API key

alternatives.name: Gemini Notebook
alternatives.desc: Upload the sources, ask for the draft, and click the citations when the machine gets confident.

facts.install: Sign in with a Google account at notebooklm.google.com or install the official mobile app
facts.engines: Google Gemini models; Google says Gemini 3.1 Pro is available in NotebookLM/Gemini Notebook, with other media features using additional Google models
facts.dataFormat: Each notebook and its copied or auto-synced source files live in the user's Google account/cloud and now sync with Gemini; imported Drive files remain linked for refresh, while direct uploads are stored as notebook sources
facts.gapVsPaid: It is excellent for source-grounded research, but not a complete marketing writer with SEO optimization, revision controls, brand governance, and publishing.
facts.setupBlocker: Setup is clean, but every source must be uploaded or imported and sensitive material is entrusted to Google's cloud

alternatives.name: Vane
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted answer engine that searches the live web and shows its receipts; it researches better than it manages content.

facts.install: Run the official Docker image with one command; it bundles Vane and SearXNG
facts.engines: Local models through Ollama plus OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Groq and other cloud providers; web search through bundled SearXNG
facts.dataFormat: Search history and uploads are stored in the mounted local Docker volume; prompts leave the host only when a cloud model is selected
facts.gapVsPaid: It can return cited research and reports, but it lacks Writesonic's end-to-end article editor, SEO workflow, brand controls, and campaign tooling.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker, a persistent volume and either Ollama with a downloaded model or at least one cloud-model API key

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Individual plan and a personal content workstation DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Writesonic in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and the OpenAI Responses API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: take a brief, gather user-supplied source material, generate structured article and marketing copy drafts, and keep source links, citations, and revisions attached to each section.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Build a brief form with audience, objective, tone, source URLs, and prohibited claims.
Store imported source text locally and chunk it for retrieval with SQLite FTS5.
Generate an outline first and require approval before drafting sections.
Attach source references to generated paragraphs and flag unsupported claims.
Provide rewrite controls for shorten, clarify, change tone, and add evidence.
Export clean Markdown plus a JSON research bundle.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out live search-engine rank data.
Deliberately leave out automatic publishing to third-party CMSs.
Deliberately leave out multi-user approvals and brand governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
